correctness.rationale: For positive even strictly log-concave density, any overlap of equal-radius intervals is strictly improvable by moving the fallible detector outside the perfect footprint. Any gap is strictly improvable by shifting one detector toward the prior mode. For adjoining intervals, the exact derivative normalized by density is strictly decreasing in the touching point and changes sign between zero and the radius; hence the unique global optimum up to reflection. Its root decreases with auxiliary reliability. Completing a quadratic in the Gaussian case proves the closed form. The standalone check passes 26,979 supplementary tests, which are not the global proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Existing interval rearrangement and log-concavity tools explain the proof but are not located as a published encompassing optimum theorem with the present unequal reliability and exact Gaussian root. The 2024 empirical simulation instead treats encounter-rate precision and replication rather than single-target no-false-alarm success. A yet-unlocated general sensor-placement theorem remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The literature identifies camera placement and grouping as practical monitoring choices. The theorem gives an exact universal global touching law, unique asymmetric offset and a closed normal-prior formula in a mixed reference/auxiliary design; it removes an unrestricted two-position optimization and shows precisely how reliability changes optimal placement. Explicitly limited to one target and idealized sensing rather than empirical detection-rate precision.
